chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda and Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a woman, consummated the marriage with her, and she bore him children, then he died from her. She claimed a portion of her dower from her husband's heirs, coming to seek it from them and also seeking the inheritance. He (peace be upon him) said: As for the inheritance, she may seek it. As for the dower, it is that which she took from the husband before he consummated the marriage with her; that is what made her private part permissible to him, whether it was little or much. When she took possession of it from him, accepted it, and went to him (to live with him), she has nothing else after that.
ai.seo_question: What are the dower and inheritance rights of a wife if her husband dies after consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that upon the husband's death after consummation, the wife is entitled to both her inheritance share and the full dower (mahr) she received prior to entering the marital bed, as this amount constitutes the price of her permissibility. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the initial dower and any additional compensation, emphasizing that once the wife accepts the initial dower and enters the husband's presence, her financial claim regarding the dower is fully satisfied. This hadith serves as a key precedent in al-Kafi for resolving disputes between the wife and the husband's heirs regarding outstanding dower payments.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, and Jameel Bin Salih, from Al Fuzayl,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who married a woman and copulated with her, or made her a mother, then died from her. So she claimed something from her dower upon the inheritors of her husband. So she came over seeking from them and sought the inheritance (as well). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the inheritance, so it is for her if she were to seek it, and as for the dower, so it is that which she took from her husband before he had copulated with her, it being that which made her to be Permissible for her husband, whether it was little or more. When she took possession of it from him, and accepted, and went over to him (to live with him), and there is nothing for her after that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘ Ubaydah and Jamil ibn Salih from al-Fudayl who has said the following: “About the case of a man who marries a woman, goes to bed with her, makes her to give birth to children, then dies and she asks something of her mahr (dower) from the heirs of the deceased as well as her share of inheritance, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

She can ask for her share of inheritance but mahr (dower) is what she had received from her husband before going to bed with him and that is which made their marriage lawful, whether little or more as she took possession and accepted and he went to bed with her but thereafter she has nothing to ask for.’”
